title.narrative: United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Central African Republic (MINUSCA)

description.narrative: United Nations Multi-dimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic (also called MINUSCA, which is the UN peacekeeping mission, which started in April 10th, 2014 to protect Central African Republic civilians under Chapter VII of the UN Charter. It transforms the 6,000-strong African Union-led peacekeeping force known as MISCA into a United Nations peacekeeping mission, became operational on September 15, 2014. The United Nations deployed a transition team to set up MINUSCA and prepare for a seamless transition of authority from MISCA to MINUSCA, specifically to support the transition process; facilitate humanitarian assistance; promote and protect human rights; support justice and the rule of law; disarmament; demobilization; reintegration; and repatriation processes. Funding under this activity represents Australia's assessed contribution to the operation.
